info.name: JanNet AI - API Collection
info.description:
JanNet AI civic complaint management platform — full API reference (Phase 19, SRS Section 18/20). Covers the Spring Boot backend (`{{baseUrl}}`, default `http://localhost:8080`) and the Python FastAPI AI microservice (`{{aiServiceBaseUrl}}`, default `http://localhost:8001`), as implemented through Phase 18.

AUTH MODEL:
- Backend endpoints: JWT bearer token in the `Authorization` header (`Bearer <accessToken>`), except the public Authentication endpoints explicitly marked No Auth below (register/verify-otp/resend-otp/login/mfa-verify/refresh/logout/forgot-password/reset-password — SRS 18: "all endpoints except registration, login, and OTP verification require a valid JWT", with a few additional public endpoints needed to make MFA/password-reset/logout actually reachable).
- AI service endpoints: a shared internal secret in the `X-Internal-Api-Key` header (service-to-service only, never JWT) — the caller is the Spring Boot backend itself, not an end user.

WORKFLOW: Run 'Login' (or 'Register' -> 'Verify OTP' -> 'Login' for a brand-new citizen) first and copy the returned accessToken/refreshToken into this collection's variables (or the paired environment file) before running any authenticated request. Staff-tier endpoints (Officer/Department Head/Admin/Super Admin/Verification Team) require an account with that role — self-registration only ever creates a CITIZEN account; staff accounts are provisioned via Admin > Users > Create Staff User, or the BOOTSTRAP_SUPER_ADMIN_* environment variables on a fresh database (see docker/README.md).

ERROR ENVELOPES (two distinct shapes by design — see PROJECT_INTEGRATION.md Section 2):
- Backend: `{ timestamp, status, error, message, path, details[] }` on every non-2xx JSON response (`GlobalExceptionHandler`).
- AI service: `{ error_code, message, details }` (SRS 20.6's own literal envelope for this service).

PAGINATION: List endpoints backed by Spring Data return a full Page envelope (`content`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `number`, `size`, `first`, `last`, `empty`, ...), driven by `page`/`pageSize` query parameters.

SCOPE NOTE: only endpoints that actually exist in the Phase 18 codebase are included here — no speculative/future-phase endpoints have been added. See ARCHITECTURE.md Section 8 for what each phase built and PROJECT_INTEGRATION.md Section 2 for the full, authoritative endpoint-by-endpoint contract this collection was generated from.

item.name: 4. Complaints

request.description:
CITIZEN only. multipart/form-data. Fields: photo (required, JPEG/PNG/WEBP, <=10MB), description (optional, <=500 chars) and the INCIDENT location - where the problem is, never the citizen's position at submission (V33).

New app (V33): latitude/longitude = the point the citizen confirmed on the map, locationConfirmed=true, locationSource = CAPTURE_GPS (GPS read right after an in-app camera capture) | EXIF (photo GPS) | MANUAL_PIN (pin placed by the citizen); optional detectedLatitude/detectedLongitude (automatic proposal, kept when the pin is moved), locationAccuracyMeters, photoCapturedAt (ISO-8601 with offset), submissionDistanceMeters (distance only - the citizen's own coordinates are never sent or stored). Ward fallback: locationConfirmed=true + wardId and no coordinates.

Older clients: latitude/longitude/wardId/locationSource(DEVICE_GPS) as before; the photo's own EXIF GPS now wins over DEVICE_GPS (that GPS was read when the screen opened). No coordinates: EXIF GPS, else wardId (approximate ward location).

The response's location adds source, accuracyMeters, capturedAt, detectedLatitude/Longitude, confirmedByCitizen, flags (STALE_PHOTO, LOW_ACCURACY, PIN_MOVED_FAR, NO_PHOTO_LOCATION, OUT_OF_JURISDICTION - warnings for staff, never blocking) and submissionDistanceMeters. The complaint is created at AI_PROCESSING and AI runs in the background (GAP-010). description is checked by the configurable profanity filter (GAP-054): 400 or masked.
